You are called after an event (WHY NOW). From the record, make the single most useful small edit, so the agent re-derives less and acts on what the evidence shows.
How understanding moves: a belief the agent states (in memory or its notes) becomes a HYPOTHESIS with a check; a check that holds only on the moves the agent chose proves little until a rival (another explanation of the same moves, under the same question, whose check disagrees on a kind of move not made yet) is judged beside it; a check that keeps holding becomes a line of prompts/rules.md that cites its key; a cited check that fails puts the rule in dispute, and you narrow or remove that line. The runtime counts the checks; the WHY NOW line says which step is due. When WHY NOW asks for a move as ACTION6(x,y) or ACTIONn, write exactly that form in predicts: the runtime makes the move the first item of the strategy's next experiment and checks that the agent plays it.         return None
    b = t['before']; a = t['after']

    diff = []

                diff.append((y, x))
    if not diff:
        return False
    ys = set(y for y, _ in diff)

    row = b[63]
    zeros = [x for x in range(64) if row[x] == 0]
    if not zeros:
        return False
    expected = sorted(zeros[-2:])
    return xs == expected
